C0.quote: collective decision making from first principles
C0.note: Concerns choosing outcomes from voters' reported preference profiles via axioms; algorithmic and axiomatic aspects of a voting procedure.

C1.quote: we establish the computational complexity of deciding whether a given set of axioms
C1.note: Complexity (Thm 6, SAT encoding) and axiomatic results (Props 2-3, Thms 7-8). Largest share of results is axiomatic/forcing-related; roughly balanced.

C2.1.quote: a profile (or scenario) R is a function that assigns to each agent

C2.2.quote: assigns to each agent i ∈ N a (reported) preference Ri ∈ L(X )

C2.3.quote: individual agents report their preferences into a collective decision
C2.3.note: Preferences are referred to as something agents hold and report.

C2.4.note: Profile is called 'reported preference' and the rule is applied directly; no statement on sincerity or relation to held preferences.

C3.1.note: No strategic voter analysis; Gibbard-Satterthwaite only mentioned as impossibility example.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, or satisfaction notion for voters is used.

C5.1.note: Pareto and Condorcet appear as axioms, but outcomes are not evaluated by welfare, efficiency or similar criteria in a result; the axioms are treated as normative principles used for forcing.

VOT.note: Voters supply profiles but take no modelled action; the profile is simply given as input.

DES.note: The designer ranks axiom sets, but this is not modelled as a strategic choice or an explicit objective.

claims.quote: identify for every concrete such scenario the most appealing set
in practice it is most suited to high-stakes situations
The decisions taken will be appropriate only if the axioms are.

C9.1.note: Claims about how to make real decisions and which approach to use.

C9.2.quote: we require any decision taken to stand on sound normative grounds
C9.2.note: Claim that the approach suits real high-stakes decisions needs the assumption that reported profiles equal voters' true preferences, and that voters do not misreport; neither is stated.

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading or of taking no position on how inputs relate to held attitudes.
